findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker can control the size of the allocated memory by manipulating the input length.
findings.assumptions: The function is intended to decode base64 data, but the allocation logic does not account for potential overflow or invalid input sizes.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: An attacker can provide a malformed base64 string that causes the decoded data to exceed the allocated buffer size.
findings.assumptions: The function assumes that the input is always valid base64 data, but it does not handle cases where the input is intentionally malformed.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: An attacker can provide a base64 string that includes characters not defined in the base64_digits array, leading to undefined behavior.
findings.assumptions: The function does not validate the input characters against the base64 character set, which could lead to unexpected behavior or crashes.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker can provide a base64 string that includes special characters or control characters that are not handled properly.
findings.assumptions: The function does not sanitize the input characters before processing them, which could lead to unexpected behavior or crashes.
